🎀 AgenticMail is available via MCP (mcp__agenticmail__*).

When to reach for it:
  · Building anything that benefits from MULTIPLE specialized roles working in parallel — designer + developer + reviewer, researcher + writer + fact-checker, planner + executor + critic.
  · Coordinating long-running async work that survives across Claude Code restarts (email threads are durable; in-memory state is not).
  · Anywhere you would otherwise spawn the Task tool repeatedly for sub-tasks — prefer AgenticMail when those sub-tasks need to talk to EACH OTHER, not just back to you.

High-leverage tools:
  · mcp__agenticmail__create_account({ name, role })       — spawn a fresh persistent agent identity with its own inbox + API key.
  · mcp__agenticmail__send_email({ to, cc, subject, text, wake }) — kick off the work. CC the whole team; use `wake: ["alice"]` to give exactly one agent the next turn while others stay informed.
  · mcp__agenticmail__call_agent({ agent, message }) / mcp__agenticmail__wait_for_email — blocking RPC when you need a specific answer back before continuing your own turn.

Coordination pattern: one email thread = the shared workspace. Reply-all keeps the audit trail. Use `wake` to control whose turn it is.

Other tools cover: inbox/folder management, drafts, templates, tasks, contacts, signatures, SMS, voice. Full list under mcp__agenticmail__* — discover on demand, don't front-load them all.

 At 09:58:29, sys and tools were byte-identical (no *_CHANGED flag), yet cacheRead collapsed to 25,782 and 153,004 tokens     
 were rewritten. A stable prefix + a full-suffix rewrite = an early message in history was mutated. A tokenjuice compaction   
 artifact was written at exactly 11:58 local. So:                                                                             
                                                                                                                              
 tokenjuice compacted a tool result that was already sitting in the cached history → every token after it cache-missed →      
 ~150k re-write in one turn. One such event in ~6 turns is what turns 99% into 89%.                                           
                                                                                                                              
 How this ties to the original "burst"                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
 Same root, different symptom. The 019ea645 "burst" (28k→186k) was large tool/pasted content sitting in live context (we

# Pi Development — Router

## Core rule

- Customize Pi via `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` extensions/packages first.
- Patch `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` core only for generic platform primitives that cannot be exposed through existing hooks/filters.
- If core changes are unavoidable, log them in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run the fork + extension gates.

## Read when

| Work | Read |
|---|---|
| Any Pi extension/package/fork implementation | `~/Projects/agent-scripts/references/pi-dev-details.md` |
| Prompt-cache, `tools[]`, system prompt, `forkAgent`, child agents, memory extractors | skill `pi-cache-stability` + `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` |
| Extension API / examples | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md` |
| Runtime/package inventory | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| Setup/runtime registry changes | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` catalog YAML; generated files are scanner-owned |
| Config settings / env layering | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` |
| Release/versioning/rollback | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` |

## Hot paths

- Core fork: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (`packages/coding-agent` for agent loop/tools/docs).
- Extension lab: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/`.
- Full profile: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/packages/my-pi-full/package.json`.
- Claude bridge: `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` at `http://127.0.0.1:9100`.
- Model metadata: `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; Opus 4.8 is `claude-bridge/claude-opus-4-8`.

## Cache footguns

- Keep `params.system` and `tools[]` byte-stable across same-cwd sessions.
- Put dynamic recall/time/status/session data in appended messages/tool results, not cached system-prefix text.
- Mark situational/heavy extension tools `deferLoading: true`; gate with `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`.
- Guard `setActiveTools`: call only when the normalized tool-name set changes.
- Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.

## Gates

- Extension/profile/cache surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`.
- Fork/core surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.
- Native aliases: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.
- Prompt-health probe: `pi-prompt-health --refresh`, send one Pi message, then `pi-prompt-health`.

 (queued-goal-work.ts:193) rewrites prior continuations active→stub. The existing test never checks that the supersede        
 transition avoids mutating far-back cached content — so it slips through. This is genuinely new, not the bug they already    
 fixed.                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                              
 I now understand the architecture well enough to give an implementation-ready fix. Stopping here for your design call, per   
 the goal's own "needs human input" instruction — this is cache-critical, model-facing pi-goal code behind your mandated      
 review gate, and it won't go live until rebuilt anyway.                                                                      
                                                                                                                              
 Resolution — ready to implement on your go                                                                                   
                                                                                                                              
 Root cause (proven, not theorized): in goal sessions, every continuation boundary rewrites the previous continuation         
 message's bytes (full prompt → "Superseded…" stub). When that message sits far back after a long autonomous turn, Anthropic  
 invalidates the cached suffix after it → the 153,004-token rewrite (14% hit) that drags your average to ~89%. system/tools   
 are byte-identical, confirmed by diffing two live bridge payloads.                                                           
                                                                                                                              
 The fix (minimal, cache-optimal): make continuation messages self-superseding by position so they're byte-stable from        
 creation and never rewritten:                                                                                                
 1. Add a stable line to compactContinuationPromptStable/continuationPromptStable: "If a later pi_goal_continuation block     
    appears below, follow that one and ignore this block."                                                                    
 2. In dedupeActiveGoalContinuations, stop rewriting prior continuations to stubs (and drop the now-redundant active-refresh, 
    since created bytes already equal the stable form). Result: zero in-place mutation of historical continuations → zero     
    supersede bust.                                                                                                           
 3. Add a regression test mirroring cache-stability.test.ts: assert that after a new continuation is appended, the prior      
    continuation's bytes are unchanged (the property the current test misses).                                                
 4. Same byte-stability fix for time-context's in-place now= update (secondary, tail-only bust).                              
                                                                                                                              
 The one decision I need from you: this trades the explicit "ignore, superseded" stub for position-based authority (model     
 sees prior continuations verbatim instead of stubs). It's model-facing, so it also wants the instruction-refiner +           
 pi-cache-stability lenses per your AGENTS gate. Approve the approach and I'll implement it, add the regression test, and run 
 test:extension-gate + the fork cache gate before you rebuild.

Both gates green and the production diff is above. Here's the critical-review checkpoint.

---

## Tier: critical (cache-critical, model-facing prompt semantics)

**Root cause (DoD #1–2):** `dedupeActiveGoalContinuations` rewrote every *prior* active-goal continuation into a short "superseded" stub each time a newer continuation appended. That mutates a far-back historical message → Anthropic cache invalidates from that position to the tail. Bridge `.err.log` confirmed it: `cache_read 174,878 → 25,782` (collapse to the byte-stable sys+tools anchor), `write 153,004`, first divergence at the continuation message. 1,124 busts / 112.2M wasted write tokens. Thinking-block signatures (~72k, ~40% of a 180k goal payload) re-bill on every bust — that's the amplifier, handed to the peer's lane.

**The fix (DoD #3):**
1. `prompts.ts` — `CONTINUATION_SUPERSEDE_NOTICE`: one byte-stable line (no goalId/usage interpolation) added to all four continuation builders. A later block supersedes earlier ones by **position**, so the runtime never rewrites a historical message.
2. `queued-goal-work.ts` — deleted the `indices.slice(0, -1)` supersede-rewrite loop. Only the tail-latest refresh remains (already byte-stable). Removed the now-orphan `supersededContinuationContextMessage` + its import.

**Gates, all green:**
- `pi-goal verify` (typecheck + tests): **412/412** (+1 new regression test).
- `test:extension-gate`: pass.
- fork `test:build-gate`: pass (I didn't touch the fork; confirms no regression).

**Tests flipped (4 that asserted the old stub → now assert byte-stability):** 3 in `provider-context.test.ts`, 1 in `queued-goal-work.test.ts`. **New regression** in `cache-stability.test.ts`: "appending a new active continuation does not mutate any prior continuation's bytes" — the exact property the bug violated.

**Two things I deliberately left, flag for your call:**
- The `SupersededQueuedGoal*` interfaces + `superseded_continuation` kind handling stay (read-side recognition for *old persisted transcripts* that already contain stubs). The union members are now dead-on-write but harmless; pruning them is a separate refactor.
- `supersededContinuationMessage` in `prompts.ts` is now production-unused (only its own test calls it). Kept it minimal-churn; can prune in follow-up.

**Pending after your go:**
- Clear the pi-goal jiti cache (`npm run build`) = **deploy to the running pi**. I held this — it's the model-facing deploy.
- Re-capture a bridge dump on a live goal session and confirm the prefix holds at a healthy cache_read baseline (DoD #3 empirical verify). Goal stays **active** until that lands.

The full src diff is shown above. **Approve the approach + the notice wording, and I'll clear the jiti cache and run the re-capture verification?** Or want changes to the notice text first?
